chunks: My spy in the West has written to me informing me that some people from the people of Syria have been sent to the Season [of Hajj], who are blind of heart, deaf of hearing, and mute of sight. They seek to dress the truth with falsehood, and obey the created in disobedience to the Creator. They milk the world, extracting its milk through religion, and trade its immediate pleasures for the delayed rewards of the virtuous and God-fearing. No one will achieve success in good except he who acts for it, and no one will be recompensed for the evil except its doer.
ai.seo_question: Who are the 'blind of heart' pilgrims mentioned in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) warns the governor of Mecca about a group of Syrian pilgrims, characterized by spiritual blindness and deafness, who distort truth with falsehood and prioritize worldly gain over divine obedience. This passage highlights the early sectarian tensions and the phenomenon of using religious pilgrimage for political or material exploitation, a theme central to Shia historical analysis of the Umayyad era. The concluding maxim reinforces the principle of individual accountability, asserting that true success belongs only to those who actively perform good deeds.
